features.description: Sufficiency round tracking: every pre-impl lock run appends a durable round record to an append-only rounds ledger in plan evidence, with stable content-derived finding ids, prior-id clearance accounting, new-finding severities, and a closed per-finding class enum.
features.acceptance: a round record is appended to an append-only rounds ledger (stored beside sufficiency-findings.json in the plan's evidence directory) ONLY when the auditor actually runs — a disposition-resolution lock pass (F002/F003) never invokes the auditor and never appends an auditor round. Each round record carries the round number, the input_fingerprint, the total finding count, and per finding a TWO-LEVEL identity: a stable SEMANTIC finding id derived from the finding's locator fields (journey_id + gap_class + sorted feature_refs + a same-cell ordinal), deliberately excluding free text so a reworded or evolved finding in the same cell KEEPS its id across rounds, plus a separate content FINGERPRINT hashing the description and recommendation — material change is defined as same finding id with a different fingerprint. The record also carries which prior-round finding ids CLEARED vs PERSISTED (clearance accounting is by finding id), each new finding's severity, and each finding's class from a CLOSED enum (plan_contract / implementation_detail / editorial / scope_guard / matrix_pin). The auditor emits the class per finding via the findings schema; a missing or invalid class falls back CONSERVATIVELY to plan_contract, never silently to a disposition-eligible class. The ledger is append-only and fully reconstructable from committed evidence. Tests assert id stability when the same cell's finding is reworded (same id, new fingerprint), distinct ids for same-cell collisions, clearance accounting against a prior round, the conservative class fallback, and that a disposition-resolution pass appends no auditor round.

features.description: Convergence policy: a pure, deterministic function over the rounds ledger that decides whether the just-completed round hard-blocks, requires operator disposition, or proceeds — full clearance with only medium/low pin-class findings demands disposition instead of another paid hard block.
features.acceptance: a pure, deterministic policy function consumes the rounds ledger plus recorded dispositions and returns the gate behavior for the latest round: (a) when the round FULLY CLEARED all prior findings AND every new finding is severity medium or low AND every new finding is classed in the DISPOSITION-ELIGIBLE set {matrix_pin, implementation_detail, editorial, scope_guard}, the gate returns operator_disposition_required — the lock refuses but explicitly demands per-finding disposition (F003) rather than implying another tighten-and-paid-relock round; (b) any new high-or-critical-severity finding keeps the plain hard block; (c) any new plan_contract finding keeps the hard block, and plan_contract is neutralizable ONLY by waived_with_reason or by genuinely clearing through a plan edit — no other disposition kind bypasses it; (d) a first round with no ledger history defers to the plain gate unchanged. The verdict mapping is EXHAUSTIVE over severity x class: every combination of severity (critical/high/medium/low) and class (all five enum values, plus the unclassified->plan_contract fallback) has a defined verdict, and a test enumerates the full matrix. NO-AUDITOR RESOLUTION PATH: when the latest round's verdict was operator_disposition_required and recorded dispositions now cover every blocking finding of that round AND the plan input_fingerprint is unchanged, dontpanic plan lock proceeds by re-evaluating the EXISTING ledger and dispositions with ZERO auditor invocations — no new paid call, no new auditor round appended; a test asserts the auditor is never invoked on this path. The policy is wired into the dontpanic plan lock path and the refusal output NAMES which policy branch fired and why. The function performs no I/O beyond its arguments (no network, no filesystem, no paid calls). Tests pin all branches and assert the policy function is pure (same inputs -> same verdict).

features.description: Disposition artifact: durable per-finding operator dispositions (accepted_into_plan / deferred_to_impl / waived_with_reason / split_to_followup_plan) recorded via a CLI surface, honored by the lock path, mirrored to decisions.jsonl, and invalidated when a disposed finding recurs materially changed.
features.acceptance: per-finding operator dispositions are recorded durably in plan evidence, each one of accepted_into_plan / deferred_to_impl / waived_with_reason / split_to_followup_plan; waived_with_reason REQUIRES a non-empty reason and split_to_followup_plan REQUIRES a follow-up plan reference. Each disposition binds the finding's SEMANTIC id AND the content fingerprint it was recorded against (F001 two-level identity). PER-CLASS VALIDITY: deferred_to_impl and split_to_followup_plan are REFUSED for plan_contract-classed findings — only waived_with_reason (or an actual plan edit that clears the finding) neutralizes plan_contract; the CLI enforces this refusal. A CLI surface records dispositions against finding ids (no hand-editing of evidence files); each recorded disposition is mirrored into the plan's decisions.jsonl for the audit trail. The lock path treats a disposed finding as non-blocking with one fingerprint gate: accepted_into_plan stays BLOCKING until the plan input_fingerprint has actually changed from the one the disposition was recorded against (the operator must really edit the plan — no lock passes on an accepted-but-unedited finding), while deferred_to_impl / waived_with_reason / split_to_followup_plan suppress the block without a plan edit. STRICT INVALIDATION: a disposition is INVALIDATED whenever its finding id recurs with a content fingerprint different from the bound one — the materially changed finding re-surfaces as BLOCKING and can never hide behind the old waiver; ambiguity resolves toward blocking. Tests cover each disposition kind end-to-end through the lock path, the plan_contract per-class refusal, the accepted-but-unedited still-blocking case, the invalidation-on-change case, the missing-reason and missing-followup-ref refusals, and that an undisposed blocking finding still refuses the lock.

features.description: Dogfood against the six committed C0 rounds: replay plan 2026-06-09-001's real finding sequences as offline fixtures, asserting ledger reconstruction, full-clearance detection, per-round policy verdicts, and round-6 disposition eligibility — with zero paid auditor calls.
features.acceptance: the six committed C0 sufficiency rounds (plan 2026-06-09-001, finding counts 3 -> 2 -> 4 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5, recoverable from the plan's git evidence history) are replayed as OFFLINE fixtures. Because the historical evidence predates the class field, the fixture corpus carries EXPLICIT RETROSPECTIVE class annotations (operator-reviewed fixture metadata, clearly marked as retrospective, never produced by the auditor or the fallback path); a COMPANION test runs the same corpus WITHOUT annotations and asserts the conservative fallback classes every finding plan_contract and the policy blocks — proving the fallback and the policy independently. With annotations applied, tests reconstruct a rounds ledger from the real finding sequences, assert FULL CLEARANCE is detected at every round boundary (each round cleared 100% of the prior round's findings), and assert the policy verdict per round — every C0 round that introduced a high-severity or plan_contract-class finding verdicts as a hard block, and round 6's three medium findings (F003 purity parity = matrix_pin, F005 empty-repo wording = editorial, missing no-new-parser-extractors scope guard = scope_guard) are recognized as disposition-eligible under the eligible-class set while round 6's high tier-1 language-set finding keeps the overall block. The fixture suite makes ZERO live auditor invocations and asserts that guarantee explicitly (no paid calls under any test path).
